pl-l3d19c1-d1e117.summary: Asks how by his death we were redeemed from the devil, sin, and penalty.

pl-l3d19c1-d1e120.summary: Answers that we are freed from the devil and sin by Christ's death, since we are justified in his blood (Rom 5:9), and in being justified, i.e., freed from sins, we are freed from the devil, who held us in the chains of sins.
claims: Being freed from sin, we are freed from the devil.

pl-l3d19c1-d1e126.summary: Explains how his death frees us from sins: by it God's love is commended to us (Rom 5:8), shown to be extraordinary in handing his Son to death for sinners. Given such a pledge of love, we are moved and kindled to love God, who did so much for us, and by this we are justified, freed from sins and made just. Christ's death justifies us when charity is stirred in our hearts by it.
claims: That love kindles our love, and by it we are justified.

pl-l3d19c1-d1e136.summary: Adds a second way we are said to be justified by Christ's death: by faith in his death we are cleansed of sins.
claims: We are cleansed of sins by faith in Christ's death.

pl-l3d19c1-d1e139.summary: Supports this with Rom 3:22, 25: God's justice is through faith in Jesus Christ, whom God set forth as propitiator through faith in his blood, i.e., in his passion, as those who looked at the bronze serpent were healed. Looking with right faith at him who hung on the cross for us, we are loosed from the devil's chains, our sins, so that the devil finds nothing to punish after this life. By his death, the one true sacrifice, Christ extinguished every guilt by which the devil held us for punishment, so that he cannot prevail by tempting. He tempts as before but cannot conquer: Peter denied before Christ's death, but not after before kings. The stronger one bound the strong in our hearts, so that seduction does not follow temptation.
claims: We are freed from sins by faith in Christ's passion.
Christ's death extinguished all guilt by which the devil held us.
After Christ's death the devil tempts but cannot conquer.

pl-l3d19c1-d1e164.summary: Concludes that in Christ's blood, who paid what he did not take, we are redeemed from sin and so from the devil; as Augustine says, the invisible hostile powers are conquered where invisible desires are conquered. When guiltless blood was shed, the bonds of all the guilt by which the devil held believing debtors were blotted out; we are redeemed by him in whom the prince of this world found nothing.
claims: Christ's guiltless blood blotted out the bonds of guilt.
Conquering desires conquers the hostile powers.

pl-l3d19c1-d1e179.summary: Cites Augustine on the cause and mode of redemption: the devil found nothing in Christ to make him die, but Christ willed to die by the Father's will, tasting death from obedience and justice, not sin, and so redeemed us from the devil's slavery. We had fallen to the prince of this world, who seduced Adam and possessed us as household slaves; the Redeemer came and the deceiver was conquered. He set his cross as a mousetrap and his blood as bait; the devil shed the blood of one who owed nothing and so had to let go the debtors. The devil held us only by the chains of our sins, which the Redeemer's blood blotted out; he bound the strong man with the chains of his passion, entered his house, our hearts, seized his vessels, emptied them of bitterness, and filled them with sweetness.
claims: The devil found no cause of death in Christ.
Christ's cross was a mousetrap baited with his blood.
By killing the sinless one, the devil lost his hold on debtors.

pl-l3d19c1.summary: Asks how by Christ's death we are redeemed from the devil, sin, and penalty. Being justified in his blood, freed from sins, we are freed from the devil, who held us by sins. His death frees us from sin because it commends God's love: so great a pledge of love moves and kindles us to love God, and so we are justified. We are also justified by faith in his death, as those who looked at the bronze serpent were healed; looking at him on the cross with right faith, we are freed from sins, so that the devil finds nothing to punish and, though he still tempts, cannot conquer, as Peter shows. Augustine: the devil found nothing in Christ, yet killed him; Christ set the cross as a mousetrap baited with his blood, and by shedding the blood of one not in debt, the devil lost his debtors.
claims: Being freed from sin, we are freed from the devil, who held us by sins.
Christ's death justifies us by kindling our love for God.
Christ's death justifies us through faith in his passion.
After Christ's death the devil may tempt but cannot conquer the faithful.
The devil lost his claim on debtors by killing the sinless Christ.
